IMD Monitors Potential Cyclone Formation in Bay of Bengal; Alerts Issued for Multiple States

02 Nov 2026, 02:08 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.amarujala.com

Meteorological Developments

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has reported the formation of a low-pressure system over the Andaman Sea, which officials indicate could evolve into a cyclonic storm in the coming days. As of October 31, 2026, the system was identified as a well-marked low-pressure area over the south-east Bay of Bengal and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

According to the IMD, the system is expected to intensify into a depression within six hours and potentially develop into a cyclone within 24 hours. Current projections suggest a west-north-west trajectory, placing the system near the coast of Andhra Pradesh by the evening of November 2, 2026. The department emphasizes that the system is in an early stage, and its final trajectory and intensity remain under observation.

Potential Impact and Rainfall Forecast

While the exact path is being monitored, the IMD has issued a series of warnings for several regions across India from October 31 through November 6:

  • Coastal Alerts: Heavy rainfall is anticipated in coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh, Yanam, and Rayalaseema between November 2-3.
  • Southern India: Increased rainfall is expected in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Kerala, and Karnataka between November 2-5.
  • Central and Eastern India: Odisha is expected to experience rainfall on November 3-4, with additional precipitation likely in Telangana, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and parts of West Bengal, Bihar, and Jharkhand.
  • Northeast and North: Northern states including Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and northeastern states like Arunachal Pradesh and Assam may see light to moderate rainfall.

Advisory for Coastal Areas

Authorities have advised the following precautions:

  • Fishermen and Mariners: Vessels are urged to exercise caution due to expected rough sea conditions, with wind speeds potentially reaching 55 km/h.
  • Disaster Management: Regional governments and disaster management teams are reportedly preparing for potential inclement weather as the system matures.

How to Verify Updates

The IMD continuously updates weather data as systems evolve. For official, real-time tracking, residents and travelers are advised to monitor the official India Meteorological Department website for the latest bulletins, cyclone track maps, and localized weather warnings.
